items.t: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff, saying he went ‘too far’ and is in therapy
items.d: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Jensen Huang says he’s thankful for second chance at Nvidia employee meeting The CEO acknowledged that he had gone ‘too far’ with some of his workplace behavior and said he has been going to therapy every day, a source told NBC News. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Tech stocks take a dip as Jensen Huang comes back as Nvidia CEO 04:53 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 11:11 PM EST By Jean Lee and Jared Perlo Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around. No company has impacted the world as deeply or profoundly as Nvidia, Huang said, according to an Nvidia employee who attended the meeting. Huang called the company’s story the most interesting in the world. According to the individual, Huang expressed contrition for his past behavior and was adamant that employees should follow the company’s code of conduct. The AI hardware leader resigned from the company Nov. 12 amid mounting scrutiny about alleged romantic relationships with subordinates and Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed. According to U.S. intelligence officials, Alice Huang is suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. He also said that he has been regularly attending therapy and that he had been deeply embarrassed about recent events, the source said. The CEO was met with an overwhelmingly positive reception, even receiving a standing ovation, according to the source. Huang’s return marked a nearly unprecedented case of corporate whiplash. items.t: Trump says pardon is always an option for Huang, and that invoking the Fifth isn’t necessary
items.d: The president’s assertion that Huang does not pose a national security threat has sparked bipartisan backlash on Capitol Hill, where the Nvidia CEO is set to testify next week.
items.fullText: Donald Trump Trump says pardon is always an option for Jensen Huang, and that invoking the Fifth isn’t necessary The president’s assertion that Huang does not pose a national security threat has drawn skepticism on Capitol Hill, where the Nvidia CEO is set to testify next week. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 President Donald Trump presents the National Medal of Science to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in Washington on Oct. 8. Kent Nishimura / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 9:19 PM EST By Kyla Guilfoil President Donald Trump said that while pardoning Jensen Huang for any potential criminal activity remains an option, he doesn’t think that will be needed for the newly reinstated Nvidia CEO . “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” Trump told the New York Post in an interview published Tuesday night. Asked about Huang’s scheduled appearances next week on Capitol Hill, Trump said, “I don’t think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it’s an interesting story for people.” “I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person,” the president said. A representative for Huang declined to comment on Trump’s comments. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for further comment. Speaking at a news conference Tuesday, Attorney General Todd Blanche indicated he would have told Trump if Huang had been involved in any criminal activity. “To the extent that, that the department, that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said. President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he’d spoken to Blanche and “they did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he himself was exonerated,” referring to Huang. Asked at an unrelated press conference about Trump’s remarks, Blanche said, “What the president said is that he talked to a lot of people going into the decision that he made to encourage the board to reinstate him,” before adding, “I’m not going to get into communications I have with the president about it.” He then said that what Trump was saying “is exactly right.” “To the extent that, that the department, that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said. NBC News previously reported that Trump sought Blanche and Vice President JD Vance’s help in convincing Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back. An administration official said the attorney general told the president that the DOJ had no evidence of wrongdoing by Huang or the company. items.fullText: NVIDIA and Microsoft Expand Accelerated Computing From Azure to Windows PCs NVIDIA and Microsoft expand tools for enterprises to customize AI models and deploy applications across cloud and local infrastructure. November 19, 2026 by Dave Salvator 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA and Microsoft are extending their full-stack collaboration to help organizations build, customize and deploy intelligent applications — from next-generation infrastructure on Azure to industrial systems and Windows PCs. At Microsoft Ignite , the companies are expanding access to Azure virtual machines powered by NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, as well as adding customer availability to NVIDIA open models and customization capabilities through Microsoft Foundry, and new options for running AI at the edge, where businesses generate and use their data. Microsoft is also using NVIDIA technologies to accelerate its own models and services, including NVIDIA Dynamo inference software for post-training and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs for Bing search models. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Running in Azure NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems are running in Azure data centers , providing infrastructure designed for demanding reasoning, agentic applications, and large-scale model training and inference. Microsoft and NVIDIA are also collaborating to extend confidential computing to bare-metal and rack-scale AI infrastructure. The work will help protect sensitive models and data while they are being processed, supporting organizations that need to work with proprietary or regulated information. NVIDIA Confidential Computing and attestation help customers verify the computing environment before releasing sensitive models, data or keys. As AI workloads span more interconnected accelerators, the companies are working to extend those protections across the AI factory infrastructure. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. November 18, 2026 by Justin Walker 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work. Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC. A Windows PC Built for Local AI As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system. Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks. items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. items.fullText: NVIDIA DGX Spark Developer Kit Turns a Desk Into a Supercomputing Lab Build and test scientific applications by connecting up to four NVIDIA DGX Spark systems for a combined 512GB of shared memory, without waiting for a spot on shared systems. November 16, 2026 by Allen Bourgoyne 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems , each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming soon. Researchers get a place at their desk to run multi-node scientific workloads, AI models and agents, instead of waiting for time on a shared GPU cluster. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks. A Supercomputing Lab on Any Desk The DGX Spark Developer Kit changes how researchers work. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 It scales from one system, or node, to four — linked directly to one another over NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking, with no network switch to buy or set up. At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 16TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1. With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises. items.fullText: How the World’s Most Advanced AI Infrastructure Supply Chain Invents the Future Over two decades running the most complex manufacturing on the planet, NVIDIA operations chief Deb Shoquist has required three things of every supply chain partner: extreme technical skill, unshakeable trust and a willingness to always try something new. November 16, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. Shoquist meets with key suppliers quarterly and spends six weeks each year on the road visiting partners in Taiwan, China, Korea, Vietnam and the U.S., where conversations move from meeting rooms to factory floors
